title: Epigenetic clock analysis of diet, exercise, education, and lifestyle factors
abstract: )-an indicator of fruit and vegetable consumption, whereas intrinsic epigenetic age acceleration (IEAA) is associated with poultry intake (p=0.03) and BMI (p=0.05). Both EEAA and IEAA were also found to relate to indicators of metabolic syndrome, which appear to mediate their associations with BMI. Metformin-the first-line medication for the treatment of type 2 diabetes-does not delay epigenetic aging in this observational study. Finally, longitudinal data suggests that an increase in BMI is associated with increase in both EEAA and IEAA.Overall, the epigenetic age analysis of blood confirms the conventional wisdom regarding the benefits of eating a high plant diet with lean meats, moderate alcohol consumption, physical activity, and education, as well as the health risks of obesity and metabolic syndrome.

claims.text: Lower extrinsic epigenetic age acceleration (EEAA) is significantly associated with greater intake of fish.
Lower EEAA is significantly associated with higher educational attainment.
Lower EEAA is significantly associated with lower body mass index (BMI).
Lower EEAA is significantly associated with current alcohol drinker status.
Lower intrinsic epigenetic age acceleration (IEAA) is significantly associated with greater poultry intake.
Lower IEAA is significantly associated with lower BMI.
Longitudinal increase in BMI is significantly associated with an increase in EEAA.
Longitudinal increase in BMI is significantly associated with an increase in IEAA.
Metformin use does not delay epigenetic aging rates in blood in this observational cohort study.
EEAA is positively associated with plasma levels of C-reactive protein (CRP).
EEAA is positively associated with the number of metabolic syndrome symptoms.
IEAA is positively associated with the number of metabolic syndrome symptoms.

limitations.text: Self-reported lifestyle and dietary habits from food frequency questionnaires are subject to reporting bias and inaccuracy, potentially causing false negative results.
Small sample sizes in specific sub-analyses, such as the 11 longitudinal participants who initiated metformin, limit statistical power to detect modest anti-aging effects.
The observational design assumes non-confounding from unmeasured variables such as pre-existing comorbidities and cannot definitively establish direct causality.
Findings from WHI did not fully validate in the InCHIANTI cohort due to demographic, cultural, dietary assessment, and sample size differences.

future_work.text: Revisit whether metformin affects epigenetic aging rates in blood or other tissues using randomized controlled trials or larger prospective sample sizes.
Conduct larger longitudinal studies to dissect causal relationships between epigenetic aging rates, dietary measures, education, exercise, and lifestyle factors.

methodologies.name: Intrinsic and Extrinsic Epigenetic Age Acceleration Analysis
methodologies.description: Calculation of DNA methylation age and residual age acceleration measures (IEAA and EEAA) using Illumina Infinium 450K methylation arrays combined with blood cell count estimations and multivariable linear meta-analyses.
conditions: Adjusted for dataset, sex, chronological age, and ethnicity
